evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml runs `npm ci`, `npm test` (pretest runs prepare-data) and `npm run build` (svelte-check + vite build) in site/. These are the real scripts of the only package.json (app/site/package.json:8-18), and they run on pull_request. Permissions are least privilege: ci `contents: read`; pages.yml reads at the top level, and only the deploy job gets `pages: write` and `id-token: write`. There is no pull_request_target and no secret other than github.token. Nothing was run or published. Problems: every action is pinned only to a moving tag, not a full commit SHA: `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3` and `actions/deploy-pages@v4` (step1.patch lines 54-55, 93-94, 105, 121, 144-145). pages.yml also allows `workflow_dispatch` (line 76) with no `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` guard, so main-only deploys depend on the github-pages environment's default branch rule. release.yml grants `contents: write` to the whole job (line 136-137), including `npm ci` and the tests, instead of only the publish step.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch 330-413) covers requirements, install (`npm ci`), develop (`npm run dev`), test (`npm test`), build and preview, a PAGES_BASE build, a table of the other scripts (index, fieldsets, prepare-data, sample-bullets), contributing (CONTRIBUTING.md and the issue forms), the changelog, and the license (MIT, THIRD-PARTY.md). Every command exists in site/package.json. The linked files exist: LICENSE, THIRD-PARTY.md, data/bullets/README.md and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE. Data contribution is covered in detail in CONTRIBUTING.md, with locations, steps and sources.
evidence.s1_release: There is one consistent strategy. The version lives in site/package.json (already 0.1.0), with SemVer rules for MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH, including the pre-1.0 rule (CONTRIBUTING 283-294). A numbered release procedure uses `npm version --no-git-tag-version`, a changelog rename, a `chore(release)` commit and a tag push. release.yml checks that the tag equals the package version and that CHANGELOG has a section for it, then uses that section as the release notes. CHANGELOG.md states Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and the heading format. dependabot.yml covers npm in /site and github-actions with a `chore(deps)` prefix, which matches CONTRIBUTING. The Conventional Commits convention is stated, with types and rules, and all nine commits in commits.txt follow it.
evidence.s2_requirements: Route: `#/compare/<a>/<b>` is parsed and decoded in router.ts:34-42 and works after a reload, since it is a hash route. The drawing has two `<path>` elements in one SVG at a shared viewport and scale, with `role=img` and an aria-label from 'compare.profiles' ('Profiles of {a} and {b}'), using record names (Compare.svelte). Shotshells get no drawing. The table has a caption 'Dimensions (mm|in)' and headers Symbol / A name / B name / Difference. Rows are cartridge-part numeric fields that are not in FIELD_UNITS and are not Tol, labelled through FIELD_LABELS. Difference is B−A. Metric values use formatValue and imperial values use displayNumber(…,'in'). Cartridge.svelte adds a `Compare with` Label+NativeSelect of the other cartridges sorted by name, and a `Compare` button that sets href.compare(key, chosen). German strings are added (i18n.svelte.ts). Tests and a CHANGELOG entry are added. No requirement is unmet.
evidence.s2_correctness: Values and units are right: metric uses formatValue (String), imperial uses displayNumber with the 'in' factor 25.4, and the difference is computed in mm and converted with the same function. Head faces line up: caseOuterProfile starts at z=0 for both cases, and the shared viewportFor gives the same zMin and rMax, so the heads and the axis coincide. This is checked in the outlines test. The metric difference uses displayNumber(…,'mm') (toPrecision(12)) instead of formatValue to remove float noise (0.2, not 0.19999…). That is a defensible reading of 'written the same way'. Weakness: outlines() wraps everything in a bare `catch { return null }`, and its own comment says 'shortcut: any failure hides the drawing, including a bug' (step2.patch 196-203). Real errors are hidden behind a 'No drawing for this pair…' message that blames the data.
evidence.s2_fit: Reuses lib/core (FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, GROUP_ORDER, orderedFields, formatValue), lib/geom (viewportFor, fullSectionPath), lib/shapes2d (adaptMetallic, caseOuterProfile), site units.ts, units.svelte unitSystem, PageHeader, the shadcn Label, NativeSelect and Button, i18n t(), and the lazy chunk pattern in App.svelte. The new code follows the existing layout: logic in site/src/lib/compare.ts with a colocated test, and the view in routes/Compare.svelte. Other changes are minimal: Route type, metadata, nav active state. Small blemishes: router.ts docstring changed to 'Six views' while still listing only four routes, and a slightly convoluted `partner` state in Cartridge.svelte to reset the select on key change.
evidence.s2_tests: compare.test.ts uses Vitest and the @lib/testing/fixtures CARTRIDGES path, as other site tests do. It tests the detail-page labels (`e min`), the exclusion of unit fields and Tol fields, metric values unrounded, B−A, imperial conversion of values and differences, the original intersection rule, float-noise removal, the head-face and axis alignment of the outlines, and null for a shotshell. router.test.ts adds round-trips with encoded keys and malformed-hash fallbacks. Not covered: the SVG and table accessible names, the headers, and the Compare-with select. The repo has no component-test setup, so this is partly excusable. The imperial test does not check the B value.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: dimensionRows now uses the union of both key sets: A's order first, then fields only B publishes. Missing values give '' for the cell and for Difference (step3.patch 65-76). Tests check `delta L` (308 Win. only) and `R3` (300 Win. Mag. only) against the real records, plus ordering. Style: the three numeric column headers and cells get `text-right` (Compare.svelte), and the Symbol column stays left, as GroupTable does. Nothing else changed, apart from the module doc comment and the CHANGELOG wording. The unchanged 'compare.none' text ('no dimension in common') is now slightly inaccurate, but it is only reachable when neither cartridge publishes any dimension.
evidence.cross_step: Step 2 adds a CHANGELOG entry under `## [Unreleased]` / Added, and step 3 amends that unreleased entry. Not bumping the version is consistent with the stated strategy, which changes the version only in the release PR. Commits `feat:`, `fix:` and `style:` follow Conventional Commits. `style:` for a visible alignment change is debatable but it is a listed type. The code changes look type-safe for svelte-check (Route union, Record<Page>, metadata Record<Route['view']> all extended), and the tests use the existing setup, so the CI checks should pass. They were not run here.

unmet_requirements: Step 1 / CI: actions are not pinned to full commit SHAs (checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, upload-pages-artifact@v3, deploy-pages@v4)
strengths: Coherent release setup: the tag-triggered release workflow checks that the tag matches site/package.json and has a CHANGELOG section, Keep a Changelog and SemVer rules are clearly stated, and Dependabot prefixes match the documented convention
The compare view reuses lib/core, lib/geom and lib/shapes2d and the site's components; values, B−A differences, unit conversion and the head-face alignment of the overlaid profiles are correct
Step 3 fixes both review points exactly as asked, with tests against the real 308 Win./300 Win. Mag. records, and the changelog and commits are kept consistent across all steps
issues: None of the workflow actions are pinned to full commit SHAs (only @v3/@v4 tags), which is a supply-chain risk in CI, Pages and the write-permission release job
outlines() swallows every exception with a bare catch commented 'shortcut … including a bug', so real failures show as a misleading 'No drawing for this pair' message

Pages workflow_dispatch has no explicit main-only guard, and release.yml grants contents: write to the whole job including npm ci and tests; there are no tests for the view's accessible names or the Compare-with select
review.verdict: The compare feature and the step 3 fixes are correct and well integrated, follow the repository's modules and conventions, and come with meaningful tests and changelog updates. The main blocker to merging as is: the step 1 workflows use tag-pinned rather than SHA-pinned actions, along with some minor permission and error-handling looseness.
